quote: I don't know. I would I you know, I would just wanted to look into it.
stewart_read: Customer gave a vague, low-commitment reason for interest; rep did not probe to build an emotional anchor, just moved to roof questions.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could have been strategically avoiding over-selling before qualification, but there's no later reference to this reason, so it reads as a dropped opportunity rather than deliberate sequencing.
coaching_implication: Ask a follow-up like 'what got you thinking about it now?' to convert vague curiosity into a usable hook.

quote: just to qualify for the new furnace.
stewart_read: Rep misspoke the qualifier's purpose entirely, naming a furnace instead of solar incentives, revealing script-recitation without attention.
coaching_implication: Slow down on the qualifier script; a factual slip here compounds the customer's existing distrust of the call.

quote: And why do you need this information?
stewart_read: This is a trust/scam-adjacent objection; rep's response was a bare reassurance with no legitimacy anchor or reframe.
coaching_implication: Use protocols.how_did_you_get_my_number style specificity — reference the original form/lead source to rebuild legitimacy instead of just saying 'we're not checking into anything.'

quote: I just don't like giving out personal information to a person that calls me on the phone.
stewart_read: Second touch of the same trust objection; rep repeats nearly the same reassurance instead of trying a new angle.
coaching_implication: This is the moment to try a genuinely different angle — e.g., reduce the ask, or acknowledge the concern by name before repeating the criteria.

quote: Well, what what is the criteria? You tell me.
stewart_read: Third touch; rep answers the literal question (criteria) but still doesn't address the underlying 'why do you need this' trust issue.
coaching_implication: Answering the surface question without addressing the root suspicion left the objection unresolved and let it escalate to termination.

quote: No. I don't wanna do this. I I don't wanna do this. I don't wanna just be giving out information.
stewart_read: Fourth and final touch — customer terminates the call; rep's repeated identical reassurance never varied enough to hold her.
coaching_implication: Four attempts, one angle. Multi_angle_resilience standard is 3+ distinct angles; this call used one angle four times.
